subject: Logs budget & tiering migration plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Logs budget & tiering migration plan

Team —

Following up from the renewal prep sync: attached is the working retention matrix (retention_matrix_v3.xlsx) that maps the current ingestion/tiering profile across Datadog, Grafana Cloud, and Sentry. The short version: our Datadog logs bill is expected to increase ~38% at current ingestion rates when we hit the next contract year unless we move 55–65% of long-tail logs to cold/archival storage and enable aggressive sampling for Sentry error events.

Asks:
- Procurement: can we approve vendor negotiations to pursue a tiered retention add-on + a 12–18 month step-down pricing commitment?
- Infra: please validate feasibility of a cold-export pipeline (GCS) and the estimated engineering runbook (approx 3–4 sprints).
- Legal/Olga: any concerns with long-term retention/export contracts and egress clauses?

I’d like to start parallel talks with Datadog and Grafana this week. I’ve flagged key line items in the sheet (hot/warm/cold thresholds, query SLA expectations).

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Infrastructure Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: retention_matrix_v3.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Logs budget & tiering migration plan

Thanks Marissa — good framing. A couple of quick notes after skimming the matrix:

- Can we get a per-tenant (top 10) ingestion delta so we can see how much is driveable by customers (app-side sampling) vs platform retention?
- For Datadog, the add-on retention tiers look like they still charge query egress per GB on cold indexes — need a clearer estimate of monthly query egress costs under our anticipated access patterns.
- If Grafana Cloud cold storage is 50% cheaper but has 6–12 hour query latency for historical searches, we should define which data classes tolerate that latency.

I’ll ask Analytics to pull the tenant-level ingestion for the last 90 days. If we can show that 20–30% is low-value debug chatter, we can make stronger concessions with vendors.

-Ben
Senior Site Reliability Engineer

Date: 2026-11-02T08:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Logs budget & tiering migration plan — Datadog quote and options

Marissa / Ben —

Appreciate the context and the sheet. I attached draft quote (dd_quote_oct2026.pdf) with two options:

1) Tiered retention add-on (12 month term) — moves 60% of indexed logs to an infrequently-searched tier with 48-hour rehydration SLA; includes 25% discount on indexed ingress for committed volume.
2) Cold archive export (GCS/ S3) — export connector + storage credits for 6 months; queries on cold data billed per TB scanned with higher latency.

A couple of clarifying points we need from you to finalize pricing: committed monthly indexed GB, typical ad-hoc historical query volume, and whether you require cross-region export.

DocuSign link for the 12-month commitment option: https://www.docusign.com/quicklink/DD-2026-1102

Happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through the SLA tradeoffs.

Best,
Alyssa Chen
Enterprise Sales, Datadog

Attachments: dd_quote_oct2026.pdf

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@datadoghq.com>, markus@grafana.com, jessica@sentry.io, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T14:33:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Logs budget & tiering migration plan — hybrid approach recommendation

Team,

After reviewing the quote + options and doing a quick cost model:

- Recommendation: Hybrid approach
  - Keep 30% of day-0 to day-7 hot indexes in Datadog (fast queries, alerts).
  - Warm: day-8 to day-30 in Datadog warm tier with reduced ingress discounts.
  - Cold: day-31+ exported to Grafana Cloud cold + GCS for long-term retention (grafana_cold_proposal.pdf). Grafana’s cold storage model gives ~60% lower storage cost vs Datadog cold and supports on-demand rehydration.
  - Sentry: enable error sampling for known noisy sources (see sentry_sampling_proposal.pdf). That should reduce Sentry ingestion by ~18–22% with minimal signal loss if we prioritize by error rate and release tagging.

What I still need from infra: realistic engineering time to build exporter + replay (we're estimating 3 sprints with 1 SRE + 1 infra eng), and from procurement: approval to negotiate a mixed-contract (Datadog retention add-on + Grafana cold export credits) rather than a single-vendor renewal.

Naomi
Director, Cost Optimization

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-05T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Approval request — move forward with tiered retention negotiations

Folks —

Summary and decision ask: after the hybrid recommendation, I want to move forward with parallel negotiations: (A) lock a 12-month Datadog retention add-on at the quoted discount tier for day-0 to day-30 classes, (B) negotiate Grafana cold export credits for day-31+ archival, and (C) enable Sentry sampling pilot for noisy projects. Procurement should push for a combined cost ceiling that keeps total logs spend growth below 12% YoY.

Olga — legal: please review the Datadog DocuSign and flag any egress/termination clauses that might lock us in on export costs.
Vivek — finance/ops: are you okay authorizing negotiation authority up to $250k annual commitment across vendors to get the blended savings?
Ben/Infra — confirm the 3-sprint engineering runbook estimate and that we can have an exporter MVP by the end of Q1.

If I don’t hear objections by EOD Wednesday (2026-11-05), I will tell vendors to proceed with final commercial proposals and push for credits/one-time onboarding discounts.

Thanks —
Marissa
